INTRODUCTIONM
Factoring polynomials is the reverse of multiplying polynomials.
Solving a polynomial equation means finding the value of the unknown.
Second degree equations often have two different values for the unknown.

FACTORING POLYNOMIALS
Factoring polynomials is the reverse of multiplying polynomials.
DISCUSSION
Both operations are based on the Distributive Property.....
Factoring involves finding two or more polynomials which can be multiplied to equal the original expression.
Polynomials are factored using these methods.
Let's start by finding the greatest common factor.
The first step in factoring a polynomial is to look for a greatest common factor (GCF) which is the largest factor common to each term.
The greatest common factor of this binomial is X since X is the largest factor common to both terms.

Now look at the signs of the trinomial. Since they are both positive, the signs of the binomials must be positive.
Look at the last term of the trinomial and list its factors.
Since (3)(1) = 3, one binomial must have a 3 and the other must have the 1.

SOLVING POLYNOMIAL EQUATIONS
Second degree equations like these have two values for the unknown.
DISCUSSION
DEFINITION
SECOND DEGREE - These are second degree equations because 2 is the greatest exponent value.
Some second degree equations may be solved by factoring the polynomial and using the Zero Product Law.
The Zero Product Law states that if the result of multiplying two real numbers is zero then at least one of the numbers must be zero.
The polynomial is factored by finding the greatest common factor.
Each factor is set equal to zero based on the Zero Product Law.
Each factor is set equal to zero based on the Zero Product Law.
